newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba and Viag make offer for Bewag - sources.
newsitem.headline: Veba and Viag make offer for Bewag - sources.

text.p: German utilities Viag AG and Veba want to make a joint bid for a higher stake in Berliner Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag) and the offer should be announced later in the day, sources said on Friday.
Sector sources said the offer for a stake of 25.5 percent in the German electricity supplier Bewag should be announced later by the state of Berlin.
The offer was not officially confirmed by either company.
A spokesman for finance minister of the state of Berlin, Annette Fugmann-Heesing of the German Social Democrat Party (SPD) said the Berlin government was currently choosing among bidders.
Sources said that nine of the 28 interested parties in Bewag were still in the running.

On Thursday Viag confirmed it was interested in increasing its stake in Bewag. Viag and Veba each already own 10 percent of Bewag's capital via subsidiaries and control 14 percent of its voting rights.
Other groups, including British electricity generator PowerGen Plc, have also expressed an interest in Bewag.
The Boersen-Zeitung newspaper earlier in the week cited Veba manager and Bewag supervisory board member Alfred Dworak as saying that Viag and Veba were interested in the stake.
Dworak told the newspaper that a joint offer would be made on Friday, with Veba aiming to take on a 14.8 percent stake and Viag 11 percent.
Whether the state of Berlin will sell more of its stake in Bewag should be decided at the start of next year.
Fugmann-Heesing favours the complete privatisation of the company, but the rest of her party has yet to make up its mind and could come to a decision when it meets in the middle of January.
The Berlin government wants the firm to be privatised by February at the latest so that the proceeds from the sale of around three billion marks can have an impact on the 1996 budget.
In the 1995/96 financial year Bewag made profits of 169 million marks.
